questions.q: What does the Sit-and-Rise test measure?
a: Getting down to the floor and back up without support
Holding your breath while standing still
Balancing on one leg with your eyes closed
Reaching your toes with straight legs
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes lowering yourself into a cross-legged seat and rising again without using hands or knees.

questions.q: What daily step count do the Starretts suggest working toward?
questions.why: Lesson 2 sets 8,000 to 10,000 steps as a solid, sustainable target for modern bodies.

questions.q: How long should you track your steps before setting a target?
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends counting from morning to night for three consecutive days to find your average.

questions.q: What Sit-and-Rise score does the summary call ideal?
questions.why: Lesson 1 starts you at 10 and deducts points for struggles or support, with a perfect 10 as the goal.

questions.q: What health benefit does the summary connect to regular squatting?
a: Up to 90% lower rates of hip arthritis
questions.why: Lesson 3 cites a study linking the squat, common in Asian cultures, to far lower rates of hip arthritis.
